subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — multilingual model fit / benchmarks (EU / APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@globexbank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — multilingual model fit / benchmarks (EU / APAC)

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

What we heard:
- Primary goal: replace a set of localized QA & customer support heuristics with a single inference pipeline that supports English + FR/DE/ES/IT and a subset of APAC languages (JA/KO/EN-IN) with consistent SLA (latency < 500ms p95 for short responses).
- Top quality concerns: mistranslation of product terms in FR/DE, polite/formal register differences in DE/FR, and entity consistency for account numbers across locales.
- Throughput target: 200 qps baseline with occasional spikes to 400 qps (end of month reporting windows).

What we proposed on the call:
- Initial model candidates & eval plan (see attached benchmarks + prompt set): lightweight LLaMA-2-13B-FT (quantized) for cost-sensitive paths, and a 70B opt-variant for high-quality fallback for EU languages; specialized tokenization and locale-specific prompt templates for FR/DE.
- Eval approach: run Redwood’s multilingual benchmark harness on your representative prompt set (attached) + your secret-test set in a secure VPC. Metrics: BLEU/ChrF for translation fidelity, locale-aware intent accuracy, and per-locale hallucination rate.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share the representative prompt set and a small secret test set (we received initial prompt bundle via attachment).
2) Redwood runs a focused eval across our candidate models and returns per-locale reports + sample responses (2 business days).
3) Sync call to review results and agree on canary plan (canary in EU region with 10% traffic, fallback policy to cheaper model variant).

Attachments: globex_prompt_set_v1.csv, redwood_multilingual_benchmarks_2026.xlsx, proposed_map_and_milestones.pdf

If that works, I’ll kick off the eval today and loop in engineering for the VPC setup.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

---
Note: We will redact any PII from your secret test set before running bench evaluations and produce a scoped SOC2 audit trail as part of the deliverable.

From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@globexbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T08:45:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — multilingual model fit / benchmarks (EU / APAC)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — that aligns with our internal view. A few clarifying q's before you start the evals: 
1) For FR/DE, do you recommend using separate locale prompt templates or a single prompt with locale hinting? Which has historically given fewer register errors?
2) Can you confirm how Redwood handles EU data residency during the evals (we prefer non-US processing for the secret test set)?
3) For the fallback policy, is there a way to specify per-intent fallback — e.g., use higher-quality model for billing/account intents, cheaper model for marketing/FAQ?

We attached a small redacted secret-test sample to the drive link. Happy for you to start on the visible prompt set immediately.

Cheers,
Emma
Emma Clarke
Head of Localization Programs
Globex Bank
emma.clarke@globexbank.com
+44 20 7946 0821

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@globexbank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — multilingual model fit / benchmarks (EU / APAC)

Emma —

Great questions. Short answers up front, details below: 
- Recommendation: start with separate locale prompt templates for FR/DE (formal variant) and a unified prompt with explicit locale hinting for APAC languages. In our experience separate templates reduce register errors by ~3–6% on Christian/academic datasets and make debugging easier.
- EU data residency: we can run the evals in our Frankfurt (eu-central-1) private cluster under your VPC — logs and artifacts remain in the EU region. We’ll provide you with the subnet and onboarding steps.
- Per-intent fallback: yes — Redwood routing policies support per-route/per-intent policies. You can map intents (billing, account, security) to stronger model variants and leave low-risk intents on the cheaper model.

Details and links: 
- Benchmarks: we’ve started runs against LLaMA-2-13B-FT (q4_0 quant) and RW-70B-opt (float16) on your prompt set; preliminary per-locale summaries are in the attached workbook. Highlights: FR/DE show higher hallucination rates on entity-heavy prompts — we recommend adding explicit entity-preservation constraints in the template (eg, "Do not invent account numbers; if unsure, ask for the last 4 digits.").
- Prompt set: the attached CSV includes locale columns and example templates. For FR/DE we suggest an alternate polite template ("Veuillez répondre en français, en utilisant un ton formel lorsqu'il s'agit de données de compte.").

I’m starting the EU-region run on the secret test set now. ETA for full per-locale report: 48 hours. I’ll follow up with a doc that maps suggested templates to intents so the engineering team can implement per-intent routing.

Best,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@globexbank.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T07:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — multilingual model fit / benchmarks (EU / APAC)

Emma / Marissa —

Quick engineering note from runtime/quality side: 
- Quantization/regression risk: when we q4_0 quantize the 13B model to save cost we see small regressions on low-resource tokenization in Korean and some Japanese honorific forms. To mitigate: 1) keep a non-quantized fallback for KO/JA intent paths; or 2) use per-locale tokenizer overrides (small extra infra complexity).
- Latency: to meet the p95 < 500ms SLA we’ll enable adaptive batching with a 50ms batching window for the EU canary. Expect slightly higher tail latency during spikes — we’ll instrument tracing so you can see per-intent p95 on the console.
- Eval artifacts: we will publish CSVs of per-example gold vs predicted, a hallucination flag column, and aggregated metrics. Rafael, can you attach the partial run output to the shared drive once it finishes?

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the per-locale error cases (I think a 20-minute review will be valuable).

– Vivek
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@globexbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — multilingual model fit / benchmarks (EU / APAC)

Hi team —

Thanks — this all sounds good. We’ve reviewed the first sheet in the benchmark workbook and the FR samples you highlighted — the entity-preservation issue shows up in ~4 of 25 examples (looks like account-number-like tokens changed). Please proceed with the EU-region secret test run and enable the per-intent fallback mapping for billing/account intents to the higher-quality variant.

Next steps for us:
- I’ll confirm a 20-minute slot on Friday for the walkthrough (please propose times).
- We’ll provision the EU VPC subnet and send the onboarding CIDR and access list by tomorrow morning.
- Rafael from our localization team will be your primary contact for additional test data.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the per-locale report.

Best,
Emma
Head of Localization Programs
Globex Bank
